nodes.source_text: Only a small overpotential of 470 mV was required to reach the OER current density of 500 mA cm⁻² in simulated seawater (1.0 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl).
It was reported to achieve 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials of 400 and 470 mV in 30 wt% KOH + 0.5 M NaCl.

nodes.description: OER performance and selectivity in seawater electrolyte
nodes.source_text: It can achieve 500 mAcm^{-2} with a small overpotential of 338 mV in 1.0 M KOH + seawater electrolyte, and exhibited almost 100% OER selectivity (Figure 3c).

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline natural seawater
nodes.source_text: It delivered a high OER current density of 500 mA cm⁻² under a low overpotential of 297 mV in alkaline natural seawater (1 M KOH + seawater).
The working potential of synthesized Ru/P-NiMoO₄@NF for UOR was 1.46 V to obtain a current density of 1000 mA cm⁻² in simulated seawater.
It can achieve 1000 mA cm⁻² at an overpotential of 341 mV in 1.0 M KOH + seawater, and was stable for over 100 h at ∼200 mA cm⁻².
Such a Cr₂O₃-CoOₓ electrode required only 1.87 V to reach 1000 mA cm⁻² at 60 °C in natural seawater electrolyzers and exhibited long-term stability of over 100 h at 500 mA cm⁻².
Co₂(OH)₃Cl exhibited a low potential of 1.63 V at 330.5 mA cm⁻² and maintained an initial current density of 99.9% after operating at ∼130 mA cm⁻² for 60000 s.
